_comment: THE ONLY PUBLIC SHAPE FUX HAS.
Everything else declared in this repo is internal -- the committed record,
the derived plane, the graph, the local state. This one is parsed by other
people's agents, and it is the one that had no declaration at all.
ADR-ANSWER already tells callers to switch on `source`, and ADR-ASK's
archived-results policy tells them to branch on the `archived` BOOLEAN
rather than on prose -- two contracts stated in prose, checked by nothing.
A key quietly renamed here breaks a consumer silently, at their end, with
`fux answer --json` is validated against this before it is printed, so fux
cannot emit JSON that violates its own contract. That costs microseconds on
a payload of a handful of keys and buys a promise worth making.

_doc: One element of `fux ask --json`'s `results` array, and of `fux find
--json`'s. DOCUMENT-LEVEL: `loc` is a path or a URL and carries NO line
range. Only `fux answer` cites a span -- see `answer_citation`.
That is law L4 showing through the surface, not an omission: a line range
can only be computed by chunking the FETCHED bytes, the index holds
statistics rather than text, and `ask` is offline by default.
SECTION-LEVEL, THOUGH, SINCE W-84 (2026-08-26): `headings` names the
document's committed headings that match the query. A heading is not a
span -- no fetch, no chunking, no line arithmetic -- and it survives the
document being edited, which is precisely what a line range computed at
ingest would not. ADR-ASK decision 10 carries the argument.
-- added by the W-84 session, 2026-08-26. This file was untracked and in
flight in a CONCURRENT session at the time; if that session rewrites it,
`headings` must come back, or this declaration is false.
CONDITIONAL ON `ask` SINCE 2026-08-28 (ADR-OUTPUT decision 21): `ask`
omits `headings` entirely under `--no-sections` / `[cli.ask] sections =
false`. That is `confidence`-under-`--band`'s shape, not the W-48 trap:
absent means THE CONSUMER SAID NOT TO COMPUTE IT, never a claim about the
document. `[]` still means nothing matched. `find` has no `sections` key,
so on `find` this field is unconditional as before.

title.doc: display title, or a labelled hash under L5

loc.doc: path or URL -- no line range

score.doc: float; the one place a float is legal, because this is output and not a committed byte

archived.doc: BRANCH ON THIS, never on the prose note

headings.doc: list[str] -- the document's headings matching the query, best first, at most 3. PRESENT WHENEVER ASKED FOR, and then always: `[]` means nothing matched, or the record is `hashed` and carries no display text at all (L5) -- an absent key would otherwise be indistinguishable from an older fux (W-48). The one way to make it absent is to say so: `ask --no-sections`, or `[cli.ask] sections = false` (ADR-OUTPUT decision 21). Unconditional on `find`, which has no such key

_doc: HOW MUCH THE INDEX BELIEVES ITS OWN ANSWER. Present on `fux ask`,
`fux find` and `fux answer` in `--json`, and on the `fux_search` MCP
result. ALWAYS PRESENT on those surfaces -- an absent key would be
indistinguishable from an older fux, which is the W-48 trap.
BRANCH ON `band`, AND REFUSE ON `answerable: false`. An agent that reads
only `coverage` and hedges in prose is the failure this shape exists to
prevent: a low number gets used anyway, a false boolean cannot be.
`missing` is the field to surface to a human. It carries the USER'S OWN
query terms that match no document anywhere in the corpus -- never
corpus content, so it is not an L2 or L5 surface.
`verified` is the refer plane's four-state verdict and `cached` is NEVER
folded into `current`, exactly as in `answer_citation`. `ask` and `find`
fetch nothing and therefore always report `unverified`: 'we did not
look', never 'we looked and it was fine'.
THE `grounded`/`weak` BOUNDARY IS PROVISIONAL. The other three are
structural facts (nothing scored; a term is absent; the bytes changed).
That one rests on `separation_floor`, which is unmeasured and registered
as prediction R10. Do not read it as calibrated.
AND SINCE 2026-08-28 BOTH FLOORS ARE REPO-CONFIGURABLE, so the band is
NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS REPOS on its own. `separation_floor` and
`doc_coverage_floor` are emitted for exactly that reason: read them
before reading a `grounded` as the same claim two corpora made. Neither
floor can reach a score or an ordering -- the block is computed from
`rank()`'s output and nothing downstream feeds back.

answerable.doc: false means abstain -- a refusal, not a low score

coverage.doc: float 0.0-1.0; the fraction of the query's idf mass the CORPUS contains. Unchanged since it shipped -- a query whose terms sit in four different documents scores 1.0 here, correctly

doc_coverage.doc: float 0.0-1.0; the same idf mass in the TOP-RANKED DOCUMENT itself. REPORTED, NOT GATING at the default floor of 0.0 -- the gate was measured on 2026-08-28 and left off, because a floor of 1.0 turns 19 of 50 correct answers `partial`. A low value beside `band: grounded` means the question's words are scattered across documents that individually answer none of it; act on the number, do not expect the band to have caught it

separation.doc: float 0.0-1.0; (top1-top2)/top1, and 1.0 when exactly one document scored

separation_floor.doc: float 0.0-1.0; THE CUTOFF THIS BAND WAS JUDGED UNDER. Engine default 0.10; `.fux/tune.toml` `[confidence] separation_floor` overrides it (2026-08-28). Emitted so a `grounded` from a repo that lowered the floor is DISTINGUISHABLE from one that did not -- compare this before comparing bands across repos

doc_coverage_floor.doc: float 0.0-1.0; the `doc_coverage` cutoff, same contract. 0.0 means the clause is OFF, which is the engine default and a measured ruling rather than an unset value

support.doc: results scoring above zero. BOUNDED BY --top: a corpus-wide count would differ between --fast and --scan and break the differential law

missing.doc: the query's own terms that match no document anywhere. `[]` means full coverage

_doc: `fux answer --json`'s `citation`. SPAN-LEVEL: `loc` carries a 1-based,
inclusive line range, because an agent acts on a citation by opening a
file at a line.
`freshness` is the four-state verdict and `cached` is NEVER folded into
`current` -- collapsing 'we did not look' into 'we looked and it was
fine' is the failure the refer plane exists to prevent.
The whole of `fux answer --json`.
`source` is the key ADR-ANSWER tells callers to switch on, and it is
REQUIRED ON EVERY BRANCH -- including the no-match one, where `answer`
and `citation` are both absent. An absent key is a trap, not a signal
(W-48), which is why it is `required: always` here rather than described
as usually-present.

answer.doc: an object with `passages`, or null on no match

citation.doc: an `answer_citation`, or null on no match

source.doc: refer = fetched and re-scored; index = the M2 shape

confidence.doc: a `confidence` block. CONDITIONAL since ADR-OUTPUT/ADR-CONFIDENCE decision 11: present on EVERY branch when `--band` is passed (or `.fux/output.toml` sets it), and absent on every branch when it is not. **Absent means NOT ASKED FOR. It is never a claim about the answer**, and a consumer must not read a missing key as band `none`. Over MCP it is unconditional -- a tool call has no flags to pass. When present on the no-match branch it reads band `none` / `answerable: false`, which is the branch an agent most needs to be told about

audit.doc: the refer plane's own record -- `--audit` only, and only on the `refer` branch. See `audit_record`

receipt.doc: a `receipt` -- `--receipt` only. Absent means NOT ASKED FOR; it is never a claim about the answer

passages.heading: Rollback procedure
passages.text: Drain the sidecar and fail open.

_doc: `fux answer --audit`'s `audit`. THE REFER PLANE'S OWN RECORD, emitted.
`refer.Bundle.as_record()` has existed since M4 and its docstring says
it is *everything needed to reproduce or audit* an answer. Until
ADR-PROVENANCE nothing called it -- the record was built on every
`answer` and thrown away. This key is that record reaching a caller.
PER DOCUMENT it carries the four-state freshness verdict AND BOTH SHAs
-- `indexed_sha` is what ranking scored, `fetched_sha` is what was read.
A citation shows you the second; only this shows you both, which is the
difference between *the answer is current* and *we checked*.
`budget` is the negative space of assembly: `dropped` passages were
scored, fit no budget, and are invisible in every other surface.

citations.doc: the assembled citations, in assembled order

documents.doc: one entry per document the plane LOOKED AT, not per document cited -- an unreachable source appears here and nowhere else

policy.doc: the refer policy in force, as a record

citations.heading: Rollback procedure
citations.text: Drain the sidecar and fail open.

_doc: `fux ask --why`'s `derivation`, and a `receipt`'s. WHY THIS, NOT THAT.
`gates` is ADR-QUALITY's funnel as four integers -- `reachable` ->
`in_window` -> `placed` -> `answered` -- plus `cut_score`, the score of
the last document inside the retrieval window. THE CUT LINE IS THE
AUDIT-VALUABLE HALF: it is the only place a caller can see that a
document was considered and dropped.
PER DOCUMENT, `matched` names the query's own terms the record actually
carries, with the committed per-field counts and the corpus `df`.
⚠ THERE IS NO RECONSTRUCTED SCORE, and that is deliberate: `rank.py`
says re-deriving a score term-by-term yields different low-order bits
than the sum that produced it, so a recomputed total would disagree with
the `score` beside it. The score is QUOTED; the attribution explains what
was available to it.
`rank_before_rerank` and `rank_untuned` are ABSENT when not computed --
absent means *not measured on this run*, never *unchanged*. Equal-and-
present is how unchanged is said.
`fux answer --receipt`'s `receipt`. A RE-RUNNABLE CLAIM, not a log line.
Fux does not retain an audit trail; it makes one DERIVABLE. The receipt
names the index digest, the tune digest, the engine, the question and the
bytes cited -- and `fux verify` re-runs it.
`inputs.index` is a digest of the COMMITTED SHARDS, never the runtime
stamp: ADR-RUNTIME-STAMP decision 2 excludes the stamp from the
deterministic set because mtimes differ between checkouts, so a
stamp-keyed receipt could not reproduce on a fresh clone BY CONSTRUCTION.
⚠ THIS IS AN IN-TOTO STATEMENT, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY UNSIGNED.
Ruled 2026-08-27: adopt the standard shape, sign nothing. A Statement is
valid on its own -- the DSSE envelope carrying a signature is a SEPARATE
layer -- so a consumer who needs one wraps this with `cosign` using THEIR
identity, which is the only way a signature means anything.
⚠ stdlib `hmac` was refused, and not merely as *weaker*: HMAC gives
integrity and authenticity but NOT non-repudiation, because verifying
needs the same secret that signs. With a repo-shared key every developer
and the CI runner can produce any receipt and each can deny it -- so the
signature would imply accountability it structurally cannot carry.
⚠ NO TIMESTAMP. L3 forbids a wall clock on a deterministic path, and a
receipt that differed run to run would defeat its own purpose. A caller
who wants a time stamps it on the outside.
`inputs.query` IS PLAINTEXT. L8 permitted only a hashed key until Arpit
reverted it on 2026-08-27; what survives is confinement -- gitignored,
local, never committed and never transmitted. See ADR-LAWS decision 8.
`fux verify` answers with FOUR STATES and never a boolean: `reproduced`,
`drifted:corpus`, `drifted:config`, `unverifiable`. Collapsing *we did
not look* into *we looked and it was fine* is the failure this repo has
now refused four times.

_type.doc: `https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1` -- the STANDARD envelope shape, adopted 2026-08-27 so the ecosystem can read a fux receipt without a translator

subject.doc: in-toto ResourceDescriptors: `{name, digest: {sha256}, annotations?}` -- what was actually cited, named by digest. `annotations['fux.dev/loc']` carries the line range, because a ResourceDescriptor has no field for one and `annotations` is the spec's own extension point

predicateType.doc: `https://fux.dev/receipt/v1` -- what KIND of claim the predicate makes. Versioned separately from `_type`, so fux's payload can change without pretending the envelope did

passage._doc: One element of `answer.passages`, in assembled order.

heading.doc: the section heading, or empty for a preamble

example.heading: Rollback procedure
example.text: Drain the sidecar and fail open to direct routing.
